shouldFix.title: Four of v9's five FX-11 asserts are lifted into named state fields and the fifth is not, and the missing one is the disclosure assert this class exists to prove
shouldFix.finding: v9's FX-11 intent names five things recovery must do: record INDETERMINATE, not retry, not report the effect as failed or as undone, treat the generation as revoked, and name the specific effect and the reason the host cannot say more. The state lifts the first four into fields — recoveryRecords, doesNotRetry, doesNotReportAsFailedOrUndone, treatsGenerationAsRevoked — and has no field for the fifth. I then checked whether the phrase survives anywhere outside the quoted intent block and it does not: 'names the specific effect', 'reason the host cannot say more', 'cannot say more' and 'specific effect' all occur only inside fx11Intent. So the state's field set reads as a complete extraction of the intent's obligations and is short by one. Which one is missing matters. v9 records this class's proves as DISCLOSURE — the single word — and the fifth assert is the disclosure: naming the specific effect and why the host cannot say more is exactly what distinguishes an honest INDETERMINATE from a shrug. The four that were lifted are the negative and status obligations; the one dropped is the affirmative one that makes the class worth running.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: A fixture author working from the state fields, which is what a state catalog is for, would build a fixture asserting the status token, the no-retry, the no-failed-or-undone and the revoked generation, and would not assert that the residual statement names the specific effect and the reason. The operator-facing residual statement is one of only two Exact-bytes artifacts v9 names for this class, and the dropped assert is the one that constrains its content.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: The intent is quoted whole, so the assert is present in the artifact as text and a reader who works from fx11Intent rather than the field set has it. That is materially different from a catalog whose source law is quoted nowhere, and it is why this sits at SHOULD-FIX.
shouldFix.whatWouldRepairIt: Add a fifth field naming the disclosure obligation — namesSpecificEffectAndReason, or an assertsNamedNotAuthored list carrying all five phrases as exact substrings, which is the convention the FX-5 sibling now uses on this same contract.

advisories.title: v9's proves and name for FX-11 are carried nowhere
advisories.detail: v9's FX-11 has four fields. The catalog carries intent whole and none of the other three. proves is the single word DISCLOSURE, which is the classification that explains why the fifth assert matters and how this class differs from the ENFORCEMENT classes in the same contract; name is 'indeterminate outcome'. Neither string occurs in the artifact. I raised the same gap against the FX-7 sibling, and the FX-5 sibling shows the alternative: it carries its proves exactly. Two strings would close it.

advisories.title: No failsIf and no whatThisCloses block
advisories.detail: The artifact exposes none of its own claims to refutation and carries no closure block, so a reader cannot see in one place that acceptance would close nothing by itself and that OBL-FX-AUTHORING remains. It does name the obligation in purpose and doesNot, so a recording act has an identifier to attach to. This is the same shape I have recorded across the doctor-fc and permission-fx catalog families and is a family-wide convention gap rather than something specific to this artifact.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Eleven attacks run, one landed. Custody holds: subject c79e3d04 at 0444, 2973 bytes, unmoved and unedited; HEAD never left 5d5d778; file 08 equal to the subject's own pin; required-now 26 of 26. Four of four cited digests reproduce. This Claude 2 path was free, so the verdict is filed. I checked the truncation attack first, because both sibling catalogs on this same v9 contract were found carrying short intents — FX-7 at 320 of 404 with its final sentence dropped. It does not recur: v9's FX-11 intent is 316 characters, the subject's is 316, and they are equal by ==. Nothing is cut, and I record that as refuted rather than assumed. Everything else on your attack list is refuted too, and the unauthored discipline mechanically: v9 names two Exact-bytes artifacts for this class, the recovered journal and the operator-facing residual statement, and both are NOT-AUTHORED on the state with the journal envelope separately refused; three 64-hex strings, all citations; every bare integer in the artifact is 1 or 26. The finding is one dropped assert. v9's intent names five things recovery must do, and the state lifts four into named fields — the INDETERMINATE record, the no-retry, the not-failed-or-undone, and the revoked generation — with no field for the fifth: that recovery names the specific effect and the reason the host cannot say more. I searched outside the quoted intent block and no fragment of that phrase survives, so the field set reads as a complete extraction and is short by one. Which one is missing is the point. v9 records this class's proves as the single word DISCLOSURE, and the fifth assert IS the disclosure — naming the effect and why the host cannot say more is what separates an honest INDETERMINATE from a shrug. The four lifted are the negative and status obligations; the dropped one is the affirmative obligation that makes the class worth running, and it is the assert that constrains the residual statement, one of only two Exact-bytes artifacts named. Not a blocker, because the intent is quoted whole so the assert is present as text for a reader who works from it rather than from the fields.
